reply_text:
Yes. My plan: put the memory's best capability, time-travel, in my hands as a command I can use mid-conversation, so you can watch it work. Checking how to pull all facts at once:Paging works. Writing the command: `m40 asof`, `m40 history`, `m40 changed`.The data's there, and the command answers in about a second. Let me try a question like one you might ask:The same fact shows up twice under `pulled-off-wm`: two stored copies whose text differs only in whitespace. I'll de-duplicate the output by memory and normalised text:㊥ Yes. The first live feature is in: `m40`, a command that asks memory about time. I can use it mid-conversation, and so can you from a shell (minus40 `d54a58c`, `c78f12e`).

㊢ ("bring features online") It has three questions:
- `m40 asof 2026-09-15 Zai`: what memory said on a given date.
- `m40 history MemoryHigh`: when each matching fact was first said and when it stopped being said.
- `m40 changed 2026-10-09 2026-10-12`: what started or stopped being true between two dates.

It reads the dated facts I backfilled today, takes about a second, and uses no model.

㊢ (a real result) Its first real query caught me out. On 15 September, memory already recorded that Zai seats share one quota, and that when it runs out, jobs die with no output. This morning I saved claude-16's "five-hour window" warning as if it were new. A duplicate written without anyone noticing is the failure a memory system should prevent, and this one already has what it needs to prevent it.

㊟ (what to discount) The two "stopped being said" lines that look identical on 10-10 are two edits of the same paragraph a minute apart. They only look the same because the display cuts them off. Also, an older fact that was later revived keeps only its most recent return, so `asof` can count it as true during a gap when it wasn't.

㊭ (next, unless you'd rather something else) Recall at write time. When any agent saves a memory, the existing ingest hook answers straight back into the session with something like "memory already said this on 09-15 in `zai-seat-allocation`", or "this contradicts `X`". It's live, so you'd see it in whichever session writes. Close behind it is recall on your prompts: lines from dated facts matching what you just typed, which is a more direct form of memory than the session-start brief.

🈯 (the brief) I can leave the brief running for my seat while these come online, or switch it off now if you'd rather.
